sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The US Food and Drug Administration ordered manufacturers of GLP-1 weight-loss and diabetes drugs, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Soliqua, to add warning labels about nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy. NAION is a rare condition caused by reduced blood flow to the optic nerve, which can lead to sudden and permanent vision loss in one eye.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: An FDA review of clinical trials and studies indicated an increased risk of NAION among GLP-1 users. However, Novo Nordisk and the American Academy of Ophthalmology noted that a direct cause-and-effect link has not been established. Patients taking these drugs often already have separate NAION risk factors, such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The American Academy of Ophthalmology advises patients not to stop taking GLP-1 medications without speaking to their doctor, and to consult an ophthalmologist immediately if sudden vision loss occurs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Kim Kardashian's Skims offered customers refunds for a $148 accessories advent calendar after online backlash. The product was mocked on social media for the low quality of its items, including hair clips and keychains.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The company acknowledged that for some customers, the calendar did not meet expectations, prompting them to contact buyers directly to offer a full refund or store credit.
